title: Brackets & Factorising Adventure
welcome_lead: Time to expand brackets, collect terms, and run the process in reverse with factorising.
meta_desc: GCSE Maths Algebra — expanding single and double brackets, collecting like terms, and basic factorising.
final_note: You can now expand a(b+c), multiply two brackets, and factorise simple expressions.

concepts.def: Multiplying out the brackets in an expression
The reverse of expanding — putting brackets back
One bracket like 3(x + 4) to multiply out
A number or letter that divides every term
First, Outer, Inner, Last — order for double brackets

walkthroughs.body_html:
To expand a(b + c), multiply a by every term inside.

3(x + 4) = 3·x + 3·4 = 3x + 12.

Watch signs: −2(x − 5) = −2x + 10. Two negatives make a plus!

For (x + a)(x + b), multiply every term in the first bracket by every term in the second.

(x + 2)(x + 3): First x·x = x². Outer x·3 = 3x. Inner 2·x = 2x. Last 2·3 = 6.

Total: x² + 5x + 6.

Find the biggest common factor of every term and pull it out.

6x + 9 → both terms divide by 3 → 3(2x + 3).

Check by expanding: 3(2x + 3) = 6x + 9. ✓

numericals.q: Factorise 10x + 15 as k(2x + 3). What is k?

free_texts.q: Expand and simplify: 2(x + 3) + 3(x − 1). Give the result.
